record.context_brief: Krylov solvability for classical Friedrichs differential operators
record.original_question: Investigate the Krylov solvability of the inverse problem Af = g for the classical Friedrichs operator on a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω ⊂ R^d defined by Af = Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k(B_k f) + C f, where each coefficient matrix B_k lies in W^{1,∞}(Ω, M_r), each B_k is self-adjoint, and C lies in L^∞(Ω, M_r) with C + C* + Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k B_k > μ 1 almost everywhere for some μ > 0. The goal is to determine what assumptions on the coefficient matrices B_k and C lead to Krylov-solvable inverse problems of this Friedrichs type.

evidence.quote: The classical Friedrichs operator on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^d with Lipschitz boundary ∂Ω is the first-order differential operator A acting as the L^2(Ω, C^r) → D'(Ω)^r map Af = Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k(B_k f) + C f for given matrix functions Bk ∈ W1,∞(Ω, Mr), k ∈ {1, . . . , d}, and C ∈ L∞(Ω, Mr) satisfying, for some μ > 0, Bk = B*k and C + C* + Σ_{k=1}^d ∂kBk > μ1 a.e. on Ω.

QUESTION 4: To investigate the Krylov-solvability of the inverse problem Af = g induced by the classical Friedrichs operator (3.1) under suitable conditions on the matrix functions matrix functions Bk ∈ W1,∞(Ω, Mr), k ∈ {1, . . . , d}, and C ∈ L∞(Ω, Mr).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, and let $r \ge 1$ be an integer. Denote by $M_r$ the space of $r \times r$ complex matrices. Consider matrix-valued coefficients $B_k \in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega, M_r)$ for $k \in \{1, \dots, d\}$ and $C \in L^\infty(\Omega, M_r)$ satisfying:
(i) $B_k(x) = B_k(x)^*$ for almost every $x \in \Omega$ and every $k$;
(ii) there exists $\mu > 0$ such that
$$C(x) + C(x)^* + \sum_{k=1}^d \partial_k B_k(x) \;\geq\; \mu\, \mathbf{1}_r \qquad \text{for a.e. } x \in \Omega.$$
Define the classical Friedrichs first-order differential operator $A$ acting from $L^2(\Omega, \mathbb{C}^r)$ to $\mathcal{D}'(\Omega)^r$ by
$$Af \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^d \partial_k(B_k f) + C f.$$
Realize $A$ as a closed densely-defined operator on the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H} := L^2(\Omega, \mathbb{C}^r)$ (with a suitable choice of domain making it boundedly invertible on its range). Given $g \in \mathrm{ran}(A)$, the inverse problem $Af = g$ is called Krylov-solvable if there exists a solution $f \in \mathcal{H}$ that lies in the closure of the Krylov subspace
$$\mathcal{K}(A,g) \;:=\; \mathrm{span}\{\, A^n g : n = 0, 1, 2, \dots \,\}.$$

Determine sufficient (and, ideally, necessary) conditions on the coefficient matrices $B_1, \dots, B_d$ and $C$ under which the inverse problem $Af = g$ associated with the Friedrichs operator $A$ above is Krylov-solvable for every $g \in \mathrm{ran}(A)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2024 survey on open problems and perspectives concerning Krylov-approximation methods for Friedrichs systems. Related works (e.g., on Krylov solvability of unbounded operators and on abstract Friedrichs systems) provide partial frameworks but do not resolve the case of the classical concrete Friedrichs differential operator on Lipschitz domains in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and perspectives on solving Friedrichs systems by Krylov approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the Krylov-solvability of inverse problems induced by classical Friedrichs operators and lists open questions on suitable conditions on the matrix coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: The Krylov-solvability question for the classical Friedrichs operator is explicitly listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Krylov Solvability of Unbounded Inverse Linear Problems
status_evidence.snippet: General framework for Krylov solvability of unbounded operator inverse problems on Hilbert spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general theory but does not resolve the concrete Friedrichs case.

status_evidence.title: Friedrichs systems on an interval
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Friedrichs systems and Krylov-type approximation in the one-dimensional setting.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on Krylov approximation for Friedrichs systems in restricted settings.
